classification.difficultyReason: Transform tangent zeros, asymptotes and branch directions, distinguish undefined endpoints from finite ones, and find new intercepts after vertical translations using standard tangent angles.

content.prompt: Sketch the graph of each of the following functions over the given intervals.

answer.short: Period $\pi$; zeros $0,\pi,2\pi$; vertical asymptotes $x=\frac\pi2,\frac{3\pi}2$. Each branch increases.
answer.worked: Use the standard tangent curve with period $\pi$. Mark zeros at $0,\pi,2\pi$ and dashed vertical asymptotes at $\frac\pi2,\frac{3\pi}2$. Draw increasing branches, tending to opposite infinities on the two sides of each asymptote. Include the endpoints $(0,0)$ and $(2\pi,0)$.

spec.description: Increasing tangent branches with two asymptotes and closed finite endpoints.

answer.short: Period $\pi$; zeros $-\pi,0,\pi$; asymptotes $x=\pm\frac\pi2$. Each branch decreases.
answer.worked: Reflect the standard tangent curve in the $x$-axis. Mark asymptotes $x=-\frac\pi2,\frac\pi2$ and zeros $-\pi,0,\pi$. Draw decreasing branches and include $(-\pi,0)$ and $(\pi,0)$.

answer.short: Period $\frac\pi2$; zeros $-\pi,-\frac\pi2,0,\frac\pi2,\pi$; asymptotes $x=\pm\frac\pi4,\pm\frac{3\pi}4$. Each branch increases.
answer.worked: The period is $\frac\pi2$. Zeros occur when $2x=k\pi$, giving $x=\frac{k\pi}2$. Asymptotes occur when $2x=\frac\pi2+k\pi$, giving $x=\frac\pi4+\frac{k\pi}2$. Mark those in $[-\pi,\pi]$, draw increasing branches, and include both finite endpoints.

spec.description: Positive tan 2x: increasing branches, correcting the answer-book reflection.

answer.short: Period $\pi$; zeros $\frac\pi2,\frac{3\pi}2$; asymptotes $x=0,\pi,2\pi$. Each branch increases.
answer.worked: Translate tangent left $\frac\pi2$. Its zeros move to $x=\frac\pi2,\frac{3\pi}2$ and its asymptotes to $x=0,\pi,2\pi$. Draw increasing branches on $(0,\pi)$ and $(\pi,2\pi)$. The function is undefined at both domain endpoints.

spec.description: Shifted tangent with asymptotes at both endpoints and π.

answer.short: Period $\pi$; zeros $\pm\frac\pi2$; asymptotes $x=-\pi,0,\pi$. Each branch decreases.
answer.worked: Translate tangent right $\frac\pi2$ and reflect in the $x$-axis. Mark zeros $-\frac\pi2,\frac\pi2$ and asymptotes $-\pi,0,\pi$. Draw decreasing branches on $(-\pi,0)$ and $(0,\pi)$. The function is undefined at the endpoints and at $0$.

spec.description: Reflected shifted tangent with central and endpoint asymptotes.

answer.worked: Translate tangent up $1$ unit. The asymptotes remain $x=\pm\frac\pi2$, and each branch increases. Plot $(-\pi,1)$, $(0,1)$ and $(\pi,1)$. Since $\tan x=-1$ at $x=-\frac\pi4,\frac{3\pi}4$, mark those two $x$-intercepts and sketch the branches.

spec.description: Tangent translated up one with closed endpoint points and y-intercept.

answer.worked: Reflect tangent in the $x$-axis, then translate up $1$. The asymptotes remain $x=\frac\pi2,\frac{3\pi}2$, and each branch decreases. Plot $(0,1)$, $(\pi,1)$ and $(2\pi,1)$. Since $\tan x=1$ at $x=\frac\pi4,\frac{5\pi}4$, mark those intercepts and sketch the branches.
